topics.title: PDF Speaker Notes
topics.text: Attach one PDF up to 100 MB to each presentation with Choose PDF, or drag one file onto Drop PDF here. Select Save Changes to upload it. Select View PDF Speaker Notes on the event detail page to open it in a new tab. Use Replace PDF or Remove current PDF on the edit page and save to update it. Use this file for notes you intend to share: anyone with its QR code can open the PDF without signing in.

topics.title: Presentation reference and file history
topics.text: Presentations record topic, date, time, speaker, duration, and expected attendance. Their dates must fit the engagement before it can be confirmed. PDF Speaker Notes and PPT Slidedeck each show the current filename, size, upload time, and uploader where available. Each presentation can hold one PDF and one .ppt or .pptx file. Older files may have no recorded uploader. Selecting a replacement PDF or PowerPoint, or checking Remove, is pending until you select Save Changes in the persistent bar at the bottom of the Edit Engagement window. This saves the entire engagement form. The notice beside the file identifies the pending change. Choose replacement or removal, not both. Cancel or leave without saving to keep the current file; after saving, check the updated filename and upload details. Speaker Notes QR links open the PDF; PPT Slidedeck QR links download the PowerPoint. Both work without signing in. Copy link shares the encoded QR address, so visits follow the same link and appear in its statistics. Merely copying a link or image adds no visit. Direct file URLs and internal QR sheets do not add visits. Changing the speaker changes a presentation's current resources; previous-speaker codes remain in historical statistics. Archive or restore presentations separately from their engagement.

topics.title: Upload or replace PDF notes and a PowerPoint
topics.text: Figure 24. Upload or replace PDF notes and a PowerPoint. Actual preview screen; fictional records. 01 In the intended numbered presentation, choose a file or drop one onto Drop PDF here or Drop PowerPoint here. PPT Slidedeck accepts .ppt and .pptx. Choosing or dropping a file does not save it. 02 PDF files may be up to 100 MB and PowerPoint files up to 500 MB. Save Changes uploads files in small chunks. Watch the progress indicator, keep the page open, and wait for saving to finish. Interrupted chunks retry automatically. 03 Use Replace PDF or Replace PPT to select an updated file. The pending notice remains until you select Save Changes in the persistent bottom bar, which saves the entire engagement form. 04 To stop sharing a file, select its Remove current checkbox, review Removal pending, then Save Changes. Choose replacement or removal, not both. The existing QR link and statistics are retained. Screenshot context: Only upload files intended for the audience: anyone with the relevant QR link can open the notes or download the PowerPoint without signing in. The retained illustration shows the file controls; the current editor also provides separate PDF and PowerPoint drop areas. Related chapters: People and organizations (p. 61) / Work queue (p. 77) / Chron and email (p. 89) / Map and calendar (p. 96)

topics.title: Speaker QR Codes
topics.text: Saving creates separate codes for each presentation's available speaker resources: website, bio, donations, connection, blog, books, custom links, notes, and PPT Slidedeck. Select a displayed code to copy its image. Select the Copy Link icon beneath a code's image to copy its web address for an email, message, or document. These controls appear when viewing or editing a presentation. Download PNG or SVG images when you prefer to save a file for your slides or handouts. File codes appear after you upload and save the corresponding PDF or PowerPoint. Replacing a file keeps its existing QR code and link, so shared slides and handouts continue to work. Removing a file hides its code; uploading it again reuses the link and its statistics. Select View QR Codes PDF, choose the codes to include, then select Prepare PDF to view, save, or print a single landscape sheet with those labeled codes, schedule, and venue. Use Select all to include every available code. Drag any code by its handle to reorder the list, whether checked or unchecked. Only checked codes appear in the PDF, in that order from left to right and then top to bottom. Keyboard users can focus a handle and press the Up or Down arrow key. Missing schedule details show To be confirmed. Disabled codes are labeled; file codes without an uploaded PDF or PowerPoint and previous speakers' codes are left out. Viewing the sheet does not add visits. Use Edit Presentations on the event's Presentations tab to open the presentation section of Edit Engagement. Numbered headings such as Presentation 1 and Presentation 2 separate the entries; check the topic and speaker before changing a file. File replacement and removal remain pending until you select Save Changes in the persistent bottom bar; the notice beside the PDF or PPT identifies the pending change. Choose replacement or removal, not both, then save and check the updated file details. Presentations can be archived and restored separately from the event. When restoring, update any date that falls outside the event's current date range. Administrators can permanently delete presentations after confirming their access; their scoped statistics reset actions appear with the saved presentation's management controls. When postponing or canceling an event, link it to a replacement from the same organization. MOED displays both "rescheduled as" and "rescheduled from" references and prevents circular links.

topics.title: Every New Event Includes Tasks We Do Not Need
topics.text: Standard Event Tasks are a customizable starting checklist. Editors and administrators can go to Work Queue > Standard Event Tasks to adjust it to the team's workflow. Edit a standard task to change its title, notes, priority, display order, or due-date rule. Due dates can be relative to the event's start or end; for example, select Event start and enter a Day offset of -7 for seven days before the start. Use + New Standard Task to add a recurring checklist item. In the Active list, use a standard task's Archive action when it should no longer be created automatically for new events. Use Restore in the Archived tab to include it in future events again. This is the shared checklist: changes apply to everyone creating events, so agree on the team's recurring needs before changing it. If a task is unnecessary for just one event, archive that event's copy in Follow-Up Work or the Work Queue. Archiving an individual event task does not disable its standard template. Likewise, archiving a standard task does not remove copies already created on existing events; archive those copies individually when appropriate. The exception is the required built-in financial closeout reminder, due one week after the event ends. It cannot be edited, archived, or deleted.

topics.title: Create a Useful Task
topics.text: 01 Write a concrete title. Use notes for supporting detail, not as a substitute for the next action. 02 Link the right record. Search for an engagement, organization, or contact; choose General MOED work when no record applies. 03 Name an owner and due date. Tasks may be unassigned or have no date, but explicit ownership keeps them out of limbo. 04 Set priority and status. Choose Low, Normal, High, or Urgent and one of the workflow states below.

topics.title: Archive tasks without changing their status
topics.text: To archive a finished item, choose Completed or canceled in the Work Queue, then Archive task. In Archived, review both badges. Restore task retains details, status, owner, and due date; completed work stays completed. An open overdue task becomes eligible for reminders again when its engagement or inquiry is also unarchived.

topics.title: Filter Work and Update Several Tasks
topics.text: Use the ownership and status/date filters to focus the Work Queue. Applied filters stay visible and are remembered in this browser; use Clear Filters to widen the view if an expected task is missing. Open a task to review its owner, due date, and status. Waiting work should name what or whom you are waiting for. For event work, check the related event and any scheduling rule before changing the date. Editors and administrators can select eligible tasks and use Complete, Reassign, or Change Due Date. Choose Preview Updates, review the selected titles and proposed change, then apply it. Tasks that changed or became ineligible are skipped and reported. Bulk completion does not send checklist emails. Use an individual task's email action when correspondence is needed, and check its delivery status.
